ideas.title: Cloudflare Workers Scheduled Triggers Never Run Because the Cron Pattern Is Missing from `wrangler.toml`
ideas.description: Why a Worker deploys successfully but its scheduled job never fires, and how to register the cron trigger correctly.
ideas.angle: Cover how Cloudflare only attaches scheduled events when the cron expression is declared in `wrangler.toml` or the dashboard, so the worker deploys without any trigger. Explain the runtime mechanism for `scheduled()` and the difference between a deployed script and an active schedule, then show the exact configuration and verification steps.

ideas.title: Bun Publishes a CLI That Runs Without `node_modules/.bin` When the Binary Field Is Wrong
ideas.description: How a Bun package can ship successfully but expose no working command because the bin entry points at the wrong file.
ideas.angle: Explain how package managers resolve the `bin` field and why a bad path or missing shebang leaves the installed command unusable. Cover Bun-specific publishing details, the executable bit, and the difference between local test runs and installed package behavior, then show how to point `bin` at the real entry file and verify it after packing.

ideas.title: Vite Builds Succeed but the Server Serves the Wrong `dist` Folder
ideas.description: Why a deployment can show an old or empty app after a successful Vite build, and how to point the server at the right output.
ideas.angle: Cover the case where the build command writes one output directory but the host, adapter, or static server serves another path. Explain how Vite emits assets, why stale build directories and mismatched root settings cause the wrong files to be served, then show how to align `root`, `build.outDir`, and the deployment target.

ideas.title: Next.js Route Handlers Throw TypeError: Body has already been read After Parsing `request.json()` Twice
ideas.description: Why a Next.js route handler fails after the request body is consumed more than once, and how to preserve the stream.
ideas.angle: Explain the fetch body model: a request stream can be consumed only once, so a second `request.json()`, `text()`, or `formData()` call throws. Cover why this happens in route handlers and middleware, then show the fix by reading once, cloning before consumption when needed, or passing the parsed object through.

drafted.title: Hono Sends an Empty Response When a Handler Forgets to Return `c.text()`
drafted.description: How a Hono route can finish without a body when the handler does not return the response object.
drafted.angle: Describe how Hono expects the handler to return a `Response` and how falling through leaves the framework with no payload to send. Explain the control flow, especially inside async handlers and middleware chains, then show the fix: return the result of `c.text()`, `c.json()`, or `await next()` appropriately.
